pdfUrls.title: PDF urls
pdfUrls.description: One pdf url per line. Each document is read once: the embedded text layer is used where a page has one, and the scans are recognised with Tesseract. A line that is not an http url, a repeat of an earlier line and a line beyond maxDocuments come back as their own free row with the reason.

maxDocuments.title: Max documents
maxDocuments.description: The list is cut here and the rest comes back free with status NOT_CHECKED_LIMIT. 0 means the default of 10, and the summary reports the number actually applied.

maxPagesPerDocument.title: Max pages per document
maxPagesPerDocument.description: Pages beyond this are not read and not charged, and the row of the last read page says how many were left. 0 means every page.

pages.title: Pages to read
pages.description: A page range like 1-5,9 for every document, or leave it empty to read from the first page. Numbering starts at 1, and a range that does not fit the document is reported in the summary.

languages.title: OCR languages
languages.description: Language packs that ship inside the image. More languages slow the recognition down, and a page in a language that is not in the list comes back with wrong words rather than with an error.

ocrMode.title: When to run OCR
enumTitles: auto: text layer first, OCR only for pages without one
always: OCR every page, ignore the text layer
never: text layer only, a page without one is free
ocrMode.description: auto is what a mixed document needs: a digital page is read exactly and instantly, and only a scanned page goes through OCR. always is for a scan wrapped in a pdf with a broken text layer. never never pays for OCR time.

dpi.title: Render DPI for OCR
dpi.description: How large a scanned page is rendered before recognition. 200 reads ordinary 10 to 12 point print; 300 helps with small print and costs roughly twice the time; below 150 small print starts to fail.

includeWords.title: Include word boxes
includeWords.description: Adds every recognised word with its box and confidence, which is what a form parser or a redaction tool needs. It makes each row several times larger, so it is off by default.
